steps.text: Heat oil in 4-quart Dutch oven over medium heat until hot. Add onion and garlic and cook for 5 minutes or until onion is tender.

Add undrained tomatoes, undrained cannellini beans, chicken broth, parsley, basil and pepper to Dutch oven and bring to a boil over high heat, stirring occasionally. Let boil for approximately 1 minute and then let simmer for 10 minutes, covered.
Add pasta to Dutch oven and simmer approximately 10 to 12 minutes or until pasta is tender. Serve immediately and enjoy.

raw_recipe.headline: Pasta e Fagioli I
raw_recipe.description: Rich and savory, a wonderful soup, it can be a meal in itself, serve with garlic toast, its great!

review.reviewBody: I'm Italian and let me tell you this is a fabulous Pasta Fagioli recipe. It is so easy and very tasty. I made the following modifications as per some of the other ratings and it came out perfect. Garlic increased from 3 to 4 cloves, used only 1 can of tomatoes (use crushed instead of stewed), increased broth to 4 cups, used 1/8 cup fresh chopped basil instead of dried, incrased pasta to 7 oz, added red pepper flakes for a little spice and topped it off with fresh grated parmesan cheese. AWESOME.

This is a wonderful recipe, I make it at least once every winter! I also add either Italian or smoked sausage and brown it with the onion and garlic. I am not a huge fan of stewed tomatoes, so sometimes I replace them with diced tomatoes (Italian style)...either way is fine. One tip I've learned, if you're planning on having leftovers, definitely do not overcook your pasta! It will absorb a lot of the broth in the fridge, and will be way too soggy and mushy.

My family really enjoys this soup. I have modified in the following manner: I use crushed tomatoes instead of stewed. I also add frozen chopped spinach instead of the parsley. Before adding the pasta [I use ditalini] I use an immersion blender to blend the beans so the soup is a little thicker. Add a salad,crusty French bread, and top with a little shredded Parm, and we're all set!

My daughter LOVES the pasta e fagioli at a local restaurant. So, I had to try to duplicate it. This recipe was a hit!! It was even better the next day! I did sweat some celery and carrots along with the onions in the beginning. I also only added 1/2 the stewed tomatoes and substituted diced tomatoes for the other 1/2 (because that's all I had). In the end, I ended up taking the large stewed tomatoes out with some liquid, puréed them, and added them back to the soup. It gave the broth a bit more body and we didn't have to eat big hunks of tomato. Next time I'll probably go with just diced tomatoes. I might add a few more beans as well. We had to sub elbows for dilatini, but it worked out great!

This dish was absolutely easy to make and rendered such a rich a savory taste. I made a few alterations as per other reviewers. I used 1 can of diced tomatoes, slightly more than 1/4 of ditalini pasta, and added about a cup of celery and carrots. Also, I did keep the pasta seperate as I didn't want it to get soggy. It came out Superb!!

So good, so easy and even better the next day - definitely add pasta as it's being eaten otherwise it gets mushy and soaks up all the juice. I did end up adding extra garlic, an extra can of tomatoes (Italian seasoned diced) along with an 8 oz can of Italian style tomato sauce; seasoned with additional freshly ground black pepper just before serving.

I perused a number of recipes and I liked the simplicity of this one. I made all the adjustments suggested by Chris from Kent, WA, except for herbs, I added the following: 1 tsp. dried of Italian seasoning, Basil, Oregano and 2 tsp. parsley. I also put the diced tomatoes (with garlic, onion, basil) in a food processor and minced (I don't like the chunks)and added mild Italian sausage. I used great northern beans plus small can of chick peas(didn't have cannellini beans). Fabulous!! Absolutely loved this soup!! I will use this recipe as my base and switch up beans, pasta, with or without for a changes in flavor.

I went slow-cooker on this and added thin-sliced celery, carrot, one small 1/4" sliced zucchini, mushrooms, and a little Italian Sausage I had left-over, (browned along with the onions and garlic) adding the less-cooked sea-shells, mushrooms and zucchini at the last 1/2 hour of cooking. OMG, GREAT!

This is the hubby's favorite soup; the entire family even my picky one wanted seconds! I stole a few tips...... 
use diced and/or crushed tomatoes,extra clove garlic, 2 cans chic broth, 4 tsp dried parsley,added 2 stalks of celery and 1 carrot.......could of used more pasta maybe 7 oz also could've used extra beans
cooked ditalini pasta separately and served by itself in a bowl then added soup.
Hubby said it was a keeper!

This is an excellent recipe. I've made it several times, using white cannellini beans, great northern and navy beans as well at different times, whatever I have on hand, soaking them overnight first. It can also be made with canned beans. I make in the slow cooker as well as a Dutch oven and either way works well. Once I even cooked it outside in the cast iron Dutch over a fire. It gets better, like most soups, stews and chilis if kept overnight. This is highly nutritious, a true comfort food and with cheese, has all food groups covered. Superb with crusty Italian bread or garlic bread.

Delicious. I used a full quart of chicken broth, diced tomatoes (undrained), 2 cans of beans (drained, but not rinsed), and less pasta, but used the seasonings called for (a touch more of each). The chicken broth and one of the cans of beans were both no-salt-added, so I did feel the need to add some salt to the soup. I let it simmer longer (about an hour) just because I wasn't ready to eat yet, and the flavours came together great. And of course I sprinkled parmesan cheese on top just before eating. Thanks for the recipe.
Tasted great
My whole family loves this recipe!
I followed the recipe and browned and added 1 lb of bulk Italian sausage to the soup. It really adds flavor. We love it!

This is delicious! I didn’t have any small pasta, so I used farfalle instead. If anyone else needs to use a larger pasta, boil it separately from the soup. All the broth was soaked up by the farfalle when I cooked it in with the fagioli. Even then it was still great! But I would not cook larger noodles in the same pot as the soup. 10/10 would soup again.
I make it all the time. I love it. My favorite!
Super easy and delicious. I used one can of stewed tomatoes in a pinch and it turned out just as good.

I added beef for a heartier soup and used spinach 
Instead of parsley. We loved it!

Amazing, a wholesome, healthy meat free option and the kids love it! Who could ask for more? The only things I added were a 1/2 tsp salt and 2 tablespoons butter to a doubled recipe for a big family. Delicious.
Oooo yummy! This is full of flavor. I used veggie broth instead of chicken broth and substituted a can of spicy tomatoes for the plain ones. This is definitely a keeper.
